body:
Elliot Price: heads up: starting to wire the model release notes section into the docs site. Need to lock a couple implementation details today: RSS/Atom feed format, nav placement, and how we handle filtering by model/version/date.

Wei Chen: yep. I’m looking at the draft from redwood-docs PR #982 (nav + per-model landing pages). Biggest question: do we have a single feed for “all model updates” + per-model feeds? Or just one?

Kira Thompson: for enterprise, both would be ideal. Some customers want an org-wide subscription, others only care about the model(s) they’ve pinned.

Tessa Morgan: from UX: I’d expect “Model release notes” in the left nav under “Models”, then within that: a list view (latest) and per-model pages. Filters should be visible, but we should avoid making the URL scheme too clever.

Elliot Price: proposal:
- Docs pages:
  - /models/release-notes (latest; filterable)
  - /models/release-notes/{model_id} (feed + page)
  - /models/release-notes/{model_id}/{version_id} (optional deep link; might just anchor on the model page)
- Feeds:
  - /models/release-notes/feed.xml (all)
  - /models/release-notes/{model_id}/feed.xml (per model)

Wei Chen: +1. Re: version filtering: do we want query params on the list view? e.g. /models/release-notes?model=rw-openllm-13b&since=2026-01-01

Elliot Price: yeah. But for canonical URLs (and SEO) I’d rather keep stable pages for per-model.

Chloe Martin: from Console side, we’re planning to link to docs via changelog_url per entry. If docs uses query params heavily, make sure the changelog_url is deterministic (no “current filters” links). We want stable permalinks for audits.

Brian Murphy: +1. Also for feeds: if we’re emitting the public JSON feed endpoint (control plane) with ETags + caching, docs can just build from that at publish time. We should avoid docs trying to “diff” anything.

Wei Chen: ok. For RSS generation, are we shipping it as part of the docs build (static) or dynamic at runtime?

Elliot Price: static at build time is simplest. But: we need it to update when new changelog entries are published, not only on full docs redeploy.

Chloe Martin: the generator pipeline already has a “docs publish job” hook (per PR #18805 in core). It can trigger a docs content sync. We can do “incremental” content update rather than full site rebuild, but depends on how redwood-docs is set up.

Wei Chen: redwood-docs is currently a full build on main. But we could do a tiny “data-only commit” that triggers the normal build. That’s acceptable if publish frequency is low (daily batch).

Kira Thompson: enterprise customers asked “near real time” but we already said batch/daily is fine for v1. Just need it to be predictable.

Elliot Price: cool. Then implement as:
- generator publishes JSON artifacts (customer-safe) to a known location (or calls a docs ingest endpoint)
- docs repo stores those artifacts under something like /content/model-release-notes/*.json
- docs site renders pages + feed from those JSON files

Wei Chen: that matches PR #982 direction. I’m starting PR #1004 for RSS/Atom generation. Need agreement on item IDs + dates.

Brian Murphy: for feed item IDs: use changelog entry ID (event_id or published_entry_id). Avoid using title text. For dates, use “published_at” not “effective_at” unless you want customers to see future-dated changes.

Kira Thompson: deprecations might be future effective dates though. But the feed entry should still show when the note was published. In the body we can include “Effective date: …”

Elliot Price: yep, publish date drives feed ordering. Effective date is a field in the content.

Tessa Morgan: version filtering on the list page: can we avoid a giant multi-select? Maybe model dropdown + “Change type” chips (perf/compat/deprecation/etc). For v1: date range + model filter is enough.

Wei Chen: re: navigation: PR #982 adds a “Release notes” child under Models, plus a right-rail “Subscribe” link. ok?

Elliot Price: yes, but careful on wording. Per style guide, call it “Model release notes” (not “Model changelog”) in docs; “changelog” is more internal jargon.

Chloe Martin: Console UI is calling the tab “Changelog” right now (design mocks). Is that a problem?

Elliot Price: not fatal but would be nicer to align. Maybe Console = “Changelog” (short) and docs = “Model release notes” (descriptive). As long as the URL works.

Wei Chen: question on version pages: do we need a dedicated /{version_id} page? Customers asked to share a single URL for the exact version they pinned.

Kira Thompson: for audit/change-management: yes, they want a permalink to a specific entry. If we can deep link to an entry ID within the model page (e.g. /{model_id}#entry-<id>) that might suffice.

Brian Murphy: +1 to anchor links. The API already gives changelog_url per entry, so make that a direct anchor. Avoid a whole extra page type unless required.

Wei Chen: ok. For the anchor we need stable DOM IDs. I’ll implement entry blocks with id="entry-{published_entry_id}".

Elliot Price: also: strict customer-safe redaction. redwood-docs PR #995 is adding a linter rule forbidding internal-only fields. We should make sure the JSON artifacts only include allowlisted fields (customer_safe_summary, impact, compatibility, deprecation timeline, links). No internal model nicknames, no vendor references.

Chloe Martin: we have an allowlist at the registry layer too (PR #260 in model registry). But +1 on docs linting as a second line of defense.

Wei Chen: version filtering detail: if the same model has multiple versions in the feed, do we group by version or by date?

Tessa Morgan: list view should be chronological by published date. Within each entry, show model + version label.

Kira Thompson: agree. And include “Hosted/Dedicated/Private availability” badges if present.

Elliot Price: availability badges: we can render from “deployment_modes” field if it’s public. If not in v1, then just text “Available in: Hosted, Dedicated” etc.

Brian Murphy: fyi, the feed endpoint PR in core (public JSON, ETags) is #18910. That can be our canonical data source if we don’t want to store JSON in the docs repo long-term.

Wei Chen: for now, storing JSON in docs repo makes reviews easy. Later we can swap to fetching from the endpoint during build.

GitHub: PR opened by Wei Chen: redwood-docs#1004 “Add RSS/Atom feed generation for model release notes”

Elliot Price: thanks. Please add:
- /models/release-notes/feed.xml (RSS)
- /models/release-notes/feed.atom (Atom)
- per-model variants under /models/release-notes/{model_id}/
And add a docs page snippet explaining how to subscribe.

Wei Chen: will do. Any requirements on max entries in feed?

Brian Murphy: keep it reasonable: last 50 entries. Add caching headers if served statically (CDN handles). If dynamic later, use ETag.

Kira Thompson: also add a note: “Feed reflects publish time; effective dates are in entry details.” This prevents confusion.

Tessa Morgan: and place “Subscribe” CTA on the list page and per-model page. Don’t hide it in the footer.

Elliot Price: action items:
- Wei: implement RSS/Atom (PR #1004), anchor IDs, max 50, subscribe CTA.
- Elliot: update nav + wording in #982, align labels.
- Chloe/Brian: confirm changelog_url format so docs can generate stable anchors (model_id + entry_id).
- Kira: sanity check enterprise wording (no internal details).

Chloe Martin: I’ll drop a proposed changelog_url format here after sync with Ethan/Brian.

Brian Murphy: draft suggestion: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/models/release-notes/{model_id}#entry-{published_entry_id}

Wei Chen: perfect.

Elliot Price: :thumbsup: let’s aim to merge #982 + #1004 by end of week, then #1017 updates Dedicated/Private docs to reference the new section.

Kira Thompson: :+1: I’ll review #1017 language once up, especially around change-management expectations.

Wei Chen: one more detail: do we need version filtering UI on the model page? like show only entries for a specific version.

Tessa Morgan: optional. If we have an anchor-per-entry, customers can search in-page. For v1 I’d skip version filter UI.

Elliot Price: agree. We can add later if customers complain.

Wei Chen: ok shipping v1 with: list page filter by model/date; model page shows all entries; deep links via anchors.

Elliot Price: done. thanks all.
